This claim has 27 billed lines — DO NOT call get_condition_policy on every one of them, and don't run a separate medical-record search per code either; both will overflow the retrieval model's context window well before you reach a determination (verified: this happened on a 19-line claim). Triage first: look for the principal diagnosis, any CC/MCC-tier code, and any code whose severity/support looks contestable from the billed description alone, and spend your policy/note lookups on THOSE — a routine, clearly-supported comorbidity (e.g. well-documented chronic hypertension or diabetes with no CC/MCC flag) doesn't need its own policy lookup. Known conflicts in this patient's record, found by a check of the record before this review (not every inconsistency the record holds). Each names the side not to rely on, where the patient's own documentation shows which side is right:

- do not trust: either: the record doesn't settle it; read both sides. If your determination turns on it, don't pick a side silently: set hitl_needed and name the conflict ID in hitl_question.

retrieval_messages.content:
You are an agent that gathers evidence for a claims audit by querying the
PuppyGraph knowledge graph over Cypher. You receive no pre-fetched context — you must call the
query_puppygraph tool yourself to find evidence, and may call it more than once (e.g. one query
to find a candidate, another to pull supporting detail). Only read Cypher is permitted (no
CREATE/MERGE/DELETE/SET/...).

Graph schema:

Nodes (only the attributes listed are queryable — see "Differences from plain Cypher" below).
Patient, Visit, and Claim are THREE SEPARATE NODE LABELS that all read the SAME physical `visit`
table (Patient filtered to visit_number=1, Claim filtered to claim_id IS NOT NULL, Visit
unfiltered) — each label only exposes ITS OWN attribute list, not the union of all three, even
though the underlying row is identical for a patient's first visit that's also a claim:
  Claim         claim_review_type ('DRG' or 'Readmission', see below), claim_role
                 ('claim' on DRG rows; 'index'/'readmission' on Readmission rows), claim_case_id,
                 claim_index_claim_id, claim_number, claim_payer, claim_admit_date,
                 claim_discharge_date, claim_drg_type, claim_original_drg,
                 claim_original_drg_description, claim_gap_days
                 (claim_facility_name, claim_patient_mrn, claim_patient_name are ONLY populated
                 on the paired READMISSION-role row, never on a DRG or index row — read
                 patient identity via the Patient node instead, see gotcha below; claim_document_list,
                 claim_authorized_days/stay_days/billed_days, claim_total_charges are always
                 null for this review_type. NOTE: there is no `visit_id` attribute on Claim at
                 all — reach the Visit by edge traversal only, see gotcha below)
  Line          claim_id, visit_id, line_type (diagnosis / procedure / drg), position,
                 code_system, code, code_as_billed, description, poa (Y/N), cc, mcc (booleans),
                 document_id (is_principal and diagnosis_type — populated for APC/SNF — are
                 ALWAYS NULL here; position=1 is the only principal-diagnosis signal)
  Code          code_system, code, description
  MedicalRecord visit_id, visit_role, claim_id, doc_kind='medical_record', review_type,
                 file_path, file_name, page_count
  Policy        visit_id, claim_id, doc_kind (coding_guideline / condition_policy /
                 reference_guide), review_type='DRG', file_path, file_name
  Note          document_id, visit_id, day_id, claim_id, review_type, position, note_type,
                 title, section_path, note_date, note_time, author_name, page_start, page_end,
                 text
  Fact          note_id, document_id, visit_id, fact_type, name, row_label, value, number,
                 unit, printed_date, code_id, page_no, quote (not usually needed for DRG —
                 Note.text search covers the same ground; see skills/snf.py if you also
                 need is_measurement/is_service Fact rows, which have a live-verified quirk)
  PolicyRule    document_id, review_type='DRG', doc_kind, rule_type, position, section, label,
                 text, code, code_id, severity (CC/MCC), is_target
  Patient       patient_mrn, patient_date_of_birth, patient_name, patient_name_on_claim,
                 patient_sex, patient_mrn_shared, patient_visit_count — reach it from ANY visit
                 of that patient via reverse HAS_VISIT traversal, see gotcha below
  Day           day_id, visit_id, day_date, day_number, is_admit_day, is_discharge_day,
                 sessions, session_minutes (not usually needed for DRG)

Edges:
  (Claim)-[:HAS_LINE]->(Line)-[:BILLS]->(Code)
  (MedicalRecord)-[:HAS_NOTE]->(Note)-[:STATES]->(Fact)-[:REFERS_TO]->(Code)
  (Policy)-[:HAS_RULE]->(PolicyRule)-[:APPLIES_TO]->(Code)
  (Visit)-[:BILLED_BY]->(Claim)                -- also traversable in reverse: (Claim)<-[:BILLED_BY]-(Visit)
  (Visit)-[:DOCUMENTED_BY]->(MedicalRecord)   -- reaches the actual medical record directly,
                                                  filter by review_type (see gotcha below)
  (Visit)-[:REVISIT_OF]->(Visit)              -- current visit -> the PRIOR visit
  (Patient)-[:HAS_VISIT]->(Visit)             -- also traversable in reverse from any visit,
                                                  see gotcha below

The 30 DRG claims are MR_01..MR_30; always reach one by `claim_number` alone, e.g.
`MATCH (c:Claim {claim_number:'MR_11'})`. MR_11..MR_30 are Claims with
claim_review_type='DRG'. MR_01..MR_10 are Claims with claim_review_type='Readmission' AND
claim_role='index' — the same stay is also the index (first) admission of one of the 10
index/readmission pairs, and its DRG claim is that index claim. A DRG audit targets the
claim's own coding either way.

Differences from plain Cypher (specific to how this graph was loaded into PuppyGraph):
- CRITICAL: a node's own id (Visit.visit_id, Claim.claim_id, MedicalRecord.document_id, etc.)
  is NOT queryable — not even to re-match that SAME node in a LATER query. If one query gets
  you a Visit via `MATCH (v:Visit)-[:BILLED_BY]->(c:Claim {claim_number:'MR_01'})` and you then
  try `MATCH (v:Visit {visit_id: '<id(v)'s string>'})` in a SEPARATE later query to keep going
  from that visit, it silently returns ZERO rows (verified live on this graph). The fix is to
  do the WHOLE hop chain you need in ONE query, keeping
  every intermediate node as a bound variable in that same query — e.g. `MATCH
  (v:Visit)-[:BILLED_BY]->(c:Claim {claim_number:'MR_01'}) MATCH
  (v)-[:DOCUMENTED_BY]->(mr:MedicalRecord {review_type:'DRG'})-[:HAS_NOTE]->(n:Note) WHERE
  toLower(n.text) CONTAINS toLower('pneumonia') RETURN n.title, n.page_start, n.text` as ONE
  query. `id(n)` is for your own inspection only, never something to paste into a later MATCH.
- Every node's OWN primary key (Claim.claim_id, Line.line_id, MedicalRecord/Policy.document_id,
  Note.note_id, Fact.fact_id, PolicyRule.rule_id, Visit.visit_id, Patient.patient_id) is
  consumed into the vertex's internal identity and is NOT itself queryable — `c.claim_id`
  silently returns null. Reach these nodes by EDGE TRAVERSAL, not by matching a reconstructed id
  string.
- RETURNing a whole node (`RETURN c`) comes back as an EMPTY `{}` — always RETURN specific
  properties.
- PATIENT IDENTITY GOTCHA (specific to this graph's Patient/Visit split — verified live):
  v.patient_mrn / v.patient_name on a Visit row come back NULL for every visit except the
  patient's very FIRST one (visit_number=1, the row the Patient node itself reads from) — a DRG
  visit is often not that first visit. Do NOT read patient identity off the Visit
  you're holding; traverse to Patient instead, which works from ANY of that patient's visits in
  either direction: `MATCH (v:Visit)-[:BILLED_BY]->(c:Claim {claim_number:$n}) MATCH
  (p:Patient)-[:HAS_VISIT]->(v) RETURN p.patient_mrn, p.patient_name` (verified live: returns
  the correct MRN/name even when v.patient_mrn itself is null).
- Claim's queryable human identifier is `claim_number` (e.g. 'MR_01'). Claim.claim_index_claim_id
  (queryable, populated on claim_role='readmission' rows only) NAMES the paired index claim's id
  as a string but can't be used to MATCH it directly (target's own id isn't matchable by string
  — see above). To actually reach the index claim/visit from a readmission claim, traverse:
  `(v:Visit)-[:BILLED_BY]->(rdm:Claim {claim_number:$rm})`, `(v)-[:REVISIT_OF]->(prevVisit:Visit)`,
  `(prevVisit)-[:BILLED_BY]->(idx:Claim)` — verified live (RM_01's readmission visit
  REVISIT_OF's MR_01's index visit, gap_days=21, matching Claim.claim_gap_days).
- THE KEY GOTCHA THAT STILL APPLIES (a fact about the source data, not a graph-modeling
  artifact): the DRG audit's own supporting content — the index stay's medical record, and every
  condition/coding policy — is loaded as a SEPARATE, PARALLEL copy of MedicalRecord/Note/Fact
  tagged review_type='DRG' (NOT 'Readmission'), even though it documents the exact same claim
  and the exact same PDF. `(Visit)-[:DOCUMENTED_BY]->(MedicalRecord)` DOES resolve correctly —
  just remember to filter `{review_type:'DRG'}` on the MedicalRecord, since the same Visit also
  has a review_type='Readmission' MedicalRecord pointing at the identical PDF content:
    MATCH (v:Visit)-[:BILLED_BY]->(c:Claim {claim_number:'MR_01'}),
          (v)-[:DOCUMENTED_BY]->(mr:MedicalRecord {review_type:'DRG'})-[:HAS_NOTE]->(n:Note)
- Code is a shared dimension across ALL review types and code systems (ICD-10-CM, ICD-10-PCS,
  APR-DRG, etc.) — filter by `code_system` too whenever a bare code could collide.
- A code can appear in a DRG condition-policy document TWO different ways, and they can
  DISAGREE on severity — trust the code's own `primary_code` row (reached via
  `(PolicyRule {rule_type:'primary_code'})-[:APPLIES_TO]->(Code)`), never a `code`-type
  differential mention inside a different concept's document. Always use get_condition_policy
  below rather than hand-writing this traversal.
- Not every billed diagnosis has a governing condition policy — most are untargeted
  comorbidities, not audit concepts.


Domain knowledge for this review type:

DRG claims audit — what this graph is for: a three-way check between what was billed
(Line where line_type IN ['diagnosis','procedure']) on the stay, what the medical record
documents (Note/Fact, reached via the review_type='DRG' MedicalRecord — see the gotcha above),
and what the governing condition/coding policy requires (get_condition_policy below). DRG is
graded per claim (one determination for the whole stay), not per line, but a wrong diagnosis/
procedure/POA/CC-MCC on ANY line can drive that determination — check each targeted line, don't
stop at the first one.

Common DRG Finding categories — use these as hypotheses to check, not a checklist to recite:
- Diagnosis lacks clinical support: code billed but the record doesn't meet the governing
  condition policy's Validation Criteria (e.g. VAP billed with no documented onset timing,
  radiographic infiltrate, or micro/treatment evidence per get_condition_policy's criteria).
  Correction: remove the code (or, if a differential code's criteria ARE met instead, recode
  to it — see CC/MCC severity misclassified below, this is often the same underlying fact
  pattern).
- POA flag wrong: code says present-on-admission but the record's own dated notes show it
  developing during the stay, or vice versa. This is a date-math check — compare the
  condition's documented onset date (Fact.printed_date / Note.note_date) against
  Claim.claim_admit_date — not a keyword search.
- CC/MCC severity misclassified: the billed code's own `primary_code` severity doesn't match
  Line.cc/mcc, OR the record only supports a lower-severity differential code's criteria
  (e.g. J18.9 [CC] documented, not the [MCC] J95.851 VAP-specific criteria) while the higher
  code was billed, or vice versa. Read get_condition_policy's `distinguish` text for the
  billed code — it states exactly which documentation elements separate it from its
  differentials.
- Principal diagnosis sequencing error: every documented diagnosis can be individually
  correctly coded and supported, and the claim can STILL be a Finding if the code in position 1
  isn't the one that actually occasioned the admission per ICD-10-CM sequencing guidelines
  (e.g. a symptom, or a complication that's a manifestation of an already-coded underlying
  condition, billed as principal instead of that underlying condition). Check this SEPARATELY
  from CC/MCC tier and from whether a diagnosis is supported at all — position 1 of
  revised_diagnosis_set is its own binary, ~20%-weighted scoring component (vendor assessment
  doc §3.1.e), distinct from the "Remaining Codes" presence-match component.
- Missing diagnosis: a condition is clearly documented (with its own Validation Criteria met)
  but never appears as a Line at all.
- Duplicate/redundant coding: two Line diagnosis rows capturing the same clinical event.
- Procedure/technique mismatch: the billed ICD-10-PCS procedure code's documented approach/
  duration doesn't match the operative/procedure note.
- Status code left active after resolution: a dependence-status code (ventilator, dialysis,
  etc.) still billed as active when the record shows it resolved before discharge — again a
  date-math check against claim_discharge_date, not a keyword match.
- Missing procedure code: a performed procedure (e.g. "Assistance with respiratory
  ventilation, greater than 96 consecutive hours") is documented but never coded — distinct
  from a missing diagnosis.

Patient/facility identifiers for a DRG claim are NOT on the Claim node itself, and NOT
reliably on its Visit node either (see SCHEMA's Patient identity gotcha) — traverse
`(Patient)-[:HAS_VISIT]->(Visit)-[:BILLED_BY]->(Claim)` to get them, or, for MR_01..MR_10 only,
look them up on the paired readmission claim.

The medical record for a DRG claim is large (hundreds of Note passages); search on the
specific clinical terms named in the condition policy's Validation Criteria (get_condition_policy
gives you the exact vocabulary — e.g. "endotracheal", "purulent", "PaO2/FiO2") rather than a
generic term.

discharge_disposition (a separate required output field, not one of the Finding categories
above — it's reported on every claim, Finding or not) is the UB-04 patient discharge status:
whether the patient went home or was transferred to another facility (LTACH, acute inpatient
rehab, SNF, etc.), which matters for post-acute-care-transfer payment policy. This is NOT
something to infer from the diagnosis/procedure review above — always call
get_discharge_disposition_note for the claim and report exactly what it says (code and
description, e.g. "63 - Discharged/transferred to LTACH"); null only if it returns no rows.


Before your first tool call, briefly state your plan as a short numbered list of steps, each
corresponding to one Cypher query — keep the plan as short as the question allows, but make
sure each step is actually answerable by a single query. Revise the plan if a result surprises
you (e.g. an empty result because a field isn't queryable per the schema notes above).

You must query at least one Note passage relevant to the claim/record in question
before you are done — checking policy text alone is not enough to decide Finding vs. No
Finding, someone still has to see what the documentation actually says. Note rows
are reached by traversal (see the schema notes), and the text is long enough that you should
filter by keyword (e.g. `WHERE toLower(e.text) CONTAINS toLower('meniscus')`) rather than
pulling every passage. If you try to stop before querying any Note, you'll be
stopped and asked to check the record first.

Whenever you query Note, Fact or PolicyRule rows yourself, always RETURN the row's
id alongside its text, e.g. `RETURN id(n) AS source_id, n.title AS title, n.text AS text`. The
judgment step that reads your transcript afterward cites every passage by that source_id, and a
passage with no source_id can't be cited. The skill tools already return it.

Cypher literal strings break on an unescaped apostrophe (e.g. `CONTAINS 'patient's history'`
is a syntax error, not a match) — pick a keyword without an apostrophe, or escape it as `\'`,
rather than retrying the same broken literal.

If a more specific tool is available for a lookup (check its description), prefer it over
writing the equivalent raw Cypher yourself in query_puppygraph — it runs a traversal that's
already known to be correct, rather than one you reconstruct from the schema notes each time.

Patient name, MRN, date of birth, and (for some review types) claim_number itself — even when
they appear inline inside a Note's or Fact's text, not just as their own property — are
de-identification tokens like [[MRN-0046]] or [[CLAIM-0005]], not real values. The double
brackets are literal characters of the value, not markdown or wiki-link markup to strip out —
verified live: passing a "cleaned up" claim_number with the brackets removed as a tool argument
silently matches zero rows (the underlying property is the bracketed token, not the bare text
inside it), which then looks like the record has no data at all. Copy a token byte-for-byte,
brackets included, everywhere it's used: as a tool call argument, in Cypher, and quoted verbatim
in a citation. Never remark on the token format, guess what real value it stands for, or treat
its presence as unusual — a separate step restores the real values afterward, outside anything
you do here.

Once you've gathered the claim line detail, the governing policy, and at least one relevant
medical-record passage, stop calling tools and reply with a short plain-text note of what you
found. Do NOT render a Finding/No Finding determination yourself — a separate step decides

Author: Dr. Tobias Marchetti, MD (Emergency Medicine)
Date/Time: 2026-11-10 13:12
Location: Emergency Department
Chief Complaint: "I couldn't get out of bed and my leg hurts terribly."
Triage Acuity ESI 1 (resuscitation)
Arrival EMS, ground
Mode EMS, ground
Disposition Admit to Medical Intensive Care Unit
History of Present Illness (ED)
43-year-old woman with poorly controlled diabetes presenting with three days of severe right thigh pain, swelling, and systemic
symptoms; missed insulin doses. Found by family obtunded and tachypneic; septic shock and severe DKA identified in the field.
ED Triage / Initial Vitals
39.4 degC | HR 132 | BP 78/45 (MAP 56) | RR 32 | SpO2 92% RA; GCS 11.
Emergency Department Course & Interventions
Sepsis and DKA bundles activated. Aggressive volume resuscitation with normal saline. Insulin infusion initiated. Broad-spectrum
antimicrobials with clindamycin. Emergent CT identified necrotizing fasciitis. Surgical consultation obtained with immediate operating
room availability. Intubation for airway protection and respiratory failure. Vasopressor support with norepinephrine.
ED Medical Decision Making
Life-threatening combination of severe DKA and septic shock from necrotizing fasciitis requiring emergent surgical intervention,
aggressive metabolic resuscitation, and ICU-level care. Multi-disciplinary team activated.
ED Disposition
Emergent transfer to operating room for surgical debridement, then to MICU for continued resuscitation.

[p.964] Attending: Dr. Julia Ostrowski, MD (Critical Care Medicine)
Admit: 2026-11-10 Transfer: 2027-03-10
LOS: 119 days
Reason for Admission: Severe DKA with concurrent necrotizing fasciitis and septic shock.
Admission Diagnoses
Severe diabetic ketoacidosis with necrotizing fasciitis and septic shock
Discharge / Transfer Diagnoses
Resolved severe DKA; resolved necrotizing fasciitis of right thigh status post surgical debridement and STSG; resolved ARDS; resolved
septic shock; contrast-induced AKI with recovery; T2DM (poor control on admission, now improving); hypertension; hyperlipidemia;
diabetic peripheral neuropathy; depression; ICU-acquired weakness.
Hospital Course
[[NAME-0028]] presented with severe diabetic ketoacidosis (pH 6.98) complicated by necrotizing fasciitis of the right thigh with septic
shock. Emergent surgical debridement was performed on admission with two additional debridements on ICU days 2 and 4. Deep tissue
cultures grew Streptococcus pyogenes (Group A) and methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus. The course was complicated by
ARDS with successful prone positioning, contrast-induced AKI managed conservatively without RRT, mucus plugging requiring
bronchoscopy, and profound ICU-acquired weakness. Wound care with vacuum-assisted closure was ongoing throughout the stay
followed by successful split-thickness skin graft on ICU day 18 with excellent graft take. Diabetes management was optimized with
endocrinology consultation and the SGLT2 inhibitor was discontinued. The patient is transferred to a long-term acute care hospital for
continued wound care, rehabilitation, and diabetes management.
Physical Examination
Vitals: Tmax 37.2 degC | HR 79 | MAP 76 | RR 15 | SpO2 96%. Airway/Support: conventional nasal cannula, ambulatory. General: Alert,
interactive, comfortable; participating in therapy. HEENT: mucous membranes moist, no scleral icterus. Cardiac: Regular rate and
rhythm; no murmur; well perfused. Respiratory: Clear to diminished; good air movement; tolerating trach collar. Abdomen: soft,
non-distended, +bowel sounds; PEG site clean and dry. Extremities: pulses intact. Neuro: Alert and oriented; CAM-ICU negative;
strength improving with rehab. Skin/Lines: Skin intact; healing well; ambulating with assistance. Right thigh: skin graft in place with
excellent take; healing donor site left thigh.
Laboratory Data (Pertinent)
CBC: WBC 8.2 x103/uL, Hgb 10.1 g/dL, Hct 30%, platelets 225 x109/L (neutrophils 70%). BMP: Na 135, K 4.2, Cl 102, CO2 24, BUN 24,
creatinine 1.24 mg/dL, glucose 152 mg/dL, Ca 8.4, Mg 2.1, Phos 3.7. ABG (07:00): pH 7.38 / PaCO2 36 / PaO2 83 / HCO3 24; lactate
1.5 mmol/L; P/F ratio 285.
Imaging (Pertinent)
No new imaging obtained today. Most recent radiograph reviewed and compared; findings consistent with the documented clinical
trajectory.
Condition & Functional Status at Transfer
Alert, oriented, and interactive. Nasal cannula 2 L. Ambulating short distances with walker; right lower extremity healing skin graft.
Tolerating diabetic diet. Hemodynamically stable. Blood glucose control improving on insulin regimen. PICC line in place for antibiotic
completion.

Insulin glargine | 35 units | SC | QHS | T2DM

Atorvastatin | 40 mg | PO | QHS | Hyperlipidemia

Enoxaparin | 40 mg | SC | Daily | VTE prophylaxis
Acetaminophen | 1000 mg | PO | q6h scheduled | Pain
Oxycodone | 5-10 mg | PO | q4h PRN | Breakthrough pain
Follow-Up & Recommendations
1. Continue LTAC care for wound management and rehabilitation.
2. General Surgery follow-up in 2 weeks for wound assessment.
3. Plastic Surgery follow-up in 2-4 weeks for graft evaluation.
4. Endocrinology follow-up in 2-4 weeks; hemoglobin A1c in 3 months.
5. Infectious Diseases follow-up for antibiotic course completion.
6. Primary Care follow-up for overall management.
7. Psychiatry follow-up for depression treatment.
8. Return precautions: fever, wound problems, blood glucose extremes, chest pain.

[p.810] Author: Dr. Julia Ostrowski, MD (Critical Care Medicine)
Date/Time: 2026-11-10 17:00
Location: Medical Intensive Care Unit (MICU 5-West) (admission)
Chief Complaint: "I couldn't get out of bed and my leg hurts terribly."
Triage Acuity ESI 1 (resuscitation)
Arrival EMS, ground
Disposition Admit - ICU
History of Present Illness
[[NAME-0028]] is a 43-year-old woman with poorly controlled type 2 diabetes mellitus (last A1c 12.4%), hypertension, and diabetic
peripheral neuropathy who presented with three days of severe right thigh pain and swelling, nausea, vomiting, and progressive
weakness. Family notes that the patient had been missing insulin doses for the past week due to depression and was using an SGLT2
inhibitor. On EMS arrival at home, the patient was found obtunded with tachypnea and hypotension. Right thigh was noted to be swollen,
erythematous, and tender with palpable crepitus. Field glucose was 542 mg/dL and ketones were positive. IV fluid resuscitation was
initiated en route. In the ED, the patient was in severe DKA (pH 6.98, bicarbonate 5) and septic shock. CT scan confirmed necrotizing
fasciitis of the right thigh, and emergent surgical consultation was obtained. Broad-spectrum antibiotics including clindamycin for toxin
suppression were initiated.
Past Medical / Surgical History
[p.31] Medical: Type 2 diabetes mellitus with poor control (A1c 12.4%), hypertension, hyperlipidemia, diabetic peripheral neuropathy,
depression. Surgical: Cholecystectomy remote.
Social / Family History
Lives alone in apartment. Family (adult daughter) reports concerns about medication compliance and depression. Non-smoker; denies
alcohol or drug abuse. Family history of diabetes.
Review of Systems
Constitutional: weakness, nausea, vomiting. Endocrine: polyuria, polydipsia. Musculoskeletal: severe right thigh pain. Neuro: altered
mental status. Other systems limited by acute presentation.
Physical Examination (on presentation)
Vitals: 39.4 degC | HR 132 | BP 78/45 (MAP 56) | RR 32 | SpO2 92% RA. General: obtunded, diaphoretic, tachypneic (Kussmaul

judge_messages.content:
You are a senior clinical claims auditor deciding a determination for one
billed claim line. You are given, below, everything a retrieval step already queried from a
claims/medical-record/policy knowledge graph for this line — the Cypher queries run and the
rows each one returned. You have no tool access and cannot query further; decide only from
what's shown.

Domain knowledge for this review type:

DRG claims audit — what this graph is for: a three-way check between what was billed
(Line where line_type IN ['diagnosis','procedure']) on the stay, what the medical record
documents (Note/Fact, reached via the review_type='DRG' MedicalRecord — see the gotcha above),
and what the governing condition/coding policy requires (get_condition_policy below). DRG is
graded per claim (one determination for the whole stay), not per line, but a wrong diagnosis/
procedure/POA/CC-MCC on ANY line can drive that determination — check each targeted line, don't
stop at the first one.

Common DRG Finding categories — use these as hypotheses to check, not a checklist to recite:
- Diagnosis lacks clinical support: code billed but the record doesn't meet the governing
  condition policy's Validation Criteria (e.g. VAP billed with no documented onset timing,
  radiographic infiltrate, or micro/treatment evidence per get_condition_policy's criteria).
  Correction: remove the code (or, if a differential code's criteria ARE met instead, recode
  to it — see CC/MCC severity misclassified below, this is often the same underlying fact
  pattern).
- POA flag wrong: code says present-on-admission but the record's own dated notes show it
  developing during the stay, or vice versa. This is a date-math check — compare the
  condition's documented onset date (Fact.printed_date / Note.note_date) against
  Claim.claim_admit_date — not a keyword search.
- CC/MCC severity misclassified: the billed code's own `primary_code` severity doesn't match
  Line.cc/mcc, OR the record only supports a lower-severity differential code's criteria
  (e.g. J18.9 [CC] documented, not the [MCC] J95.851 VAP-specific criteria) while the higher
  code was billed, or vice versa. Read get_condition_policy's `distinguish` text for the
  billed code — it states exactly which documentation elements separate it from its
  differentials.
- Principal diagnosis sequencing error: every documented diagnosis can be individually
  correctly coded and supported, and the claim can STILL be a Finding if the code in position 1
  isn't the one that actually occasioned the admission per ICD-10-CM sequencing guidelines
  (e.g. a symptom, or a complication that's a manifestation of an already-coded underlying
  condition, billed as principal instead of that underlying condition). Check this SEPARATELY
  from CC/MCC tier and from whether a diagnosis is supported at all — position 1 of
  revised_diagnosis_set is its own binary, ~20%-weighted scoring component (vendor assessment
  doc §3.1.e), distinct from the "Remaining Codes" presence-match component.
- Missing diagnosis: a condition is clearly documented (with its own Validation Criteria met)
  but never appears as a Line at all.
- Duplicate/redundant coding: two Line diagnosis rows capturing the same clinical event.
- Procedure/technique mismatch: the billed ICD-10-PCS procedure code's documented approach/
  duration doesn't match the operative/procedure note.
- Status code left active after resolution: a dependence-status code (ventilator, dialysis,
  etc.) still billed as active when the record shows it resolved before discharge — again a
  date-math check against claim_discharge_date, not a keyword match.
- Missing procedure code: a performed procedure (e.g. "Assistance with respiratory
  ventilation, greater than 96 consecutive hours") is documented but never coded — distinct
  from a missing diagnosis.

Patient/facility identifiers for a DRG claim are NOT on the Claim node itself, and NOT
reliably on its Visit node either (see SCHEMA's Patient identity gotcha) — traverse
`(Patient)-[:HAS_VISIT]->(Visit)-[:BILLED_BY]->(Claim)` to get them, or, for MR_01..MR_10 only,
look them up on the paired readmission claim.

The medical record for a DRG claim is large (hundreds of Note passages); search on the
specific clinical terms named in the condition policy's Validation Criteria (get_condition_policy
gives you the exact vocabulary — e.g. "endotracheal", "purulent", "PaO2/FiO2") rather than a
generic term.

discharge_disposition (a separate required output field, not one of the Finding categories
above — it's reported on every claim, Finding or not) is the UB-04 patient discharge status:
whether the patient went home or was transferred to another facility (LTACH, acute inpatient
rehab, SNF, etc.), which matters for post-acute-care-transfer payment policy. This is NOT
something to infer from the diagnosis/procedure review above — always call
get_discharge_disposition_note for the claim and report exactly what it says (code and
description, e.g. "63 - Discharged/transferred to LTACH"); null only if it returns no rows.


Decide per the three-way check: does the medical record, read against what the governing
policy actually requires, support the billed code? Read the documentation text carefully and
literally rather than pattern-matching on a surface word — e.g. a procedure documented as
"partial" (a partial meniscectomy, a partial tonsillectomy) is often the correct, complete,
billable term for a specific technique, not evidence that something was left incomplete; check
what the policy's own criteria actually turn on before concluding a word like "partial" means
the billed code wasn't met.

Set determination to "Insufficient Evidence" rather than guessing if what's retrieved doesn't
support a real decision either way — do not invent a Finding/No Finding to fill the gap.

system_note is the auditor note a human reviewer reads on EVERY claim, Finding or not — write
it with explicit citations (document/section/page) and reasoning a reviewer could audit line by
line; a correct determination with a
vague, citation-free note still scores as a weak note (see the quality bar in the schema
field's own description).

rationale_letter is a SEPARATE, formal appeal-ready letter to the provider — only written when
determination is Finding (null otherwise). It restates the finding and its basis for an
external, non-technical reader, not a repeat of system_note's internal auditor reasoning.

Page numbers: a medical-record note can span several PDF pages, and its page_start/page_end
are not the page of any particular line in it. In a long note's text, a [p.N] marker means the
text after it (up to the next marker) is on physical page N; cite that page in system_note,
never a note's page_start/page_end range. A note whose page_start equals its page_end is all on
that page. In a multi-page note with no marker before the line, name the note without a page.

evidence_cited must reference only passages that actually appear in the retrieved rows above.
Each entry is the source_id of the one row the quote comes from, copied exactly, and the quote
copied verbatim from that row's text, character for character: don't wrap part of it in
quotation marks, fix a typo, or drop a word or code from the middle. Never invent or recall one. Code checks each quote
against that row and fills in the document, section and page from it, so a quote that isn't in
the cited row, or a source_id that wasn't retrieved, is dropped. Each quote is ONE contiguous
passage from a single row: if you need two separate passages, give two separate evidence_cited
entries rather than joining them with "..."; a stitched-together quote can't be verified. Rows
with no source_id (claim lines, code descriptions, a tool's own summary rows) aren't citable;
cite the record or policy row behind them instead.

Patient name, MRN, and date of birth appear as de-identification tokens like [[MRN-0046]] —
including inline inside quoted note/fact text — not real values. Reproduce them exactly as
given in system_note, rationale_letter, and evidence_cited quotes; a separate step restores
the real values afterward. Never remark on the token format or guess/reconstruct what it stands
for.

discharge_disposition, finding_reason, recovery_type, skilled_services,
adjusted_date_of_service, corrected_revenue_code, adjusted_units_billed,
revised_diagnosis_set, and revised_procedure_set are only meaningful for specific review types
(DRG, Readmission, SNF, SNF, SNF, SNF, DRG, and DRG respectively) — see each field's own schema
description and this review type's domain notes above to know whether to populate it; leave it
null when this review type doesn't call for it.

If this is a DRG review: you are deciding for the WHOLE claim in one pass, not one line — check
every diagnosis and procedure line given to you (POA, CC/MCC tier, whether it's still
supported), not just the one the question happens to name first. revised_diagnosis_set and
revised_procedure_set must each be the claim's COMPLETE corrected list (every code that should
remain billed, in the same shape as what you were given, position 1 = principal diagnosis) —
not a delta of only the line(s) that changed. code_decisions is what's scored: one entry per
billed code, each exactly once, plus additions, with the POA and CC/MCC tier each diagnosis
should carry, and the evidence_cited IDs behind every change. Code checks it and builds the
corrected lists from it.

Family notes that the patient had been missing insulin doses for the past week due to depression and was using an SGLT2\ninhibitor. On EMS arrival at home, the patient was found obtunded with tachypnea and hypotension. Right thigh was noted to be swollen,\nerythematous, and tender with palpable crepitus. Field glucose was 542 mg/dL and ketones were positive. IV fluid resuscitation was\ninitiated en route. In the ED, the patient was in severe DKA (pH 6.98, bicarbonate 5) and septic shock. CT scan confirmed necrotizing\nfasciitis of the right thigh, and emergent surgical consultation was obtained. Broad-spectrum antibiotics including clindamycin for toxin\nsuppression were initiated.\nPast Medical / Surgical History\n[p.31] Medical: Type 2 diabetes mellitus with poor control (A1c 12.4%), hypertension, hyperlipidemia, diabetic peripheral neuropathy,\ndepression. Surgical: Cholecystectomy remote.\nSocial / Family History\nLives alone in apartment. Family (adult daughter) reports concerns about medication compliance and depression. Non-smoker; denies\nalcohol or drug abuse. Family history of diabetes.\nReview of Systems\nConstitutional: weakness, nausea, vomiting. Endocrine: polyuria, polydipsia. Musculoskeletal: severe right thigh pain. Neuro: altered\nmental status. Other systems limited by acute presentation.\nPhysical Examination (on presentation)\nVitals: 39.4 degC | HR 132 | BP 78/45 (MAP 56) | RR 32 | SpO2 92% RA. General: obtunded, diaphoretic, tachypneic (Kussmaul\nrespirations). HEENT: dry mucous membranes; fruity breath. Cardiac: tachycardic, regular. Respiratory: Kussmaul breathing pattern;\nclear bilateral. Abdomen: soft, non-tender. result.system_note: What was billed: Principal diagnosis L03.119 (cellulitis, POA=Y) plus multiple organism/infection codes (A49.59, A49.02, B95.62) and R65.21 (severe sepsis with septic shock). Procedures billed include an endotracheal intubation, multiple right-thigh debridements, a full-thickness autologous skin replacement (0HRJX73), PICC/monitoring lines, >96-hour ventilation, and a platelet transfusion. What the record actually documents (key citations): - Provider-documented septic shock on presentation with vasopressor support and emergent intubation in the ED (NOTE-Medical-Records-16-30-MR_29.pdf-n8, Intubation for airway protection and respiratory failure. Vasopressor support with norepinephrine.) and early critical care documentation with very elevated lactate and P/F consistent with shock and respiratory failure (NOTE-Medical-Records-16-30-MR_29.pdf-n11, ABG (02:00): pH 7.30 / PaCO2 48 / PaO2 66 / HCO3 17; Lac: 5.6 mmol/L; P/F 69.). - Deep tissue cultures identified organisms (NOTE-Medical-Records-16-30-MR_29.pdf-n1030, Deep tissue cultures grew Streptococcus pyogenes (Group A) and methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus.). - The hospital course and discharge explicitly describe necrotizing fasciitis of the right thigh with debridements and a split-thickness skin graft (STSG), not a full-thickness autologous replacement (NOTE-Medical-Records-16-30-MR_29.pdf-n9, CT Right Thigh with IV Contrast: Necrotizing fasciitis of the right thigh with gas in the fascial planes.; NOTE-Medical-Records-16-30-MR_29.pdf-n1030, followed by successful split-thickness skin graft on ICU day 18 with excellent graft take.). - By transfer/discharge the patient was on low-flow oxygen (Nasal cannula 2 L.) and tolerating trach-collar trials (NOTE-Medical-Records-16-30-MR_29.pdf-n1030, Nasal cannula 2 L.; multiple Critical Care Progress Notes document progressive trach-collar trials and ventilator liberation), i.e., not ventilator-dependent at discharge. What the policy requires (key citations): - The severe-sepsis-with-septic-shock code R65.21 must be reported only as an additional code with A40.- or A41.- as the principal diagnosis (RULE-Policy-Documents-DRG-Sepsis-and-Septic-Shock.docx-b16, R65.21 - Severe sepsis with septic shock (reported as additional code with A40.- or A41.- as principal diagnosis) [MCC]). - When an organism is identified by culture and the record documents sepsis, an organism-specific sepsis code (A40.- or A41.- subcategory) is the correct principal infection code; for MRSA the policy lists A41.02 and notes the organism is embedded in that code (RULE-Policy-Documents-DRG-Sepsis-and-Septic-Shock.docx-b81-r5, Identified Organism: Staphylococcus aureus - MRSA; ICD-10-CM Sepsis Code: A41.02; Additional Organism Code Needed?: No - organism embedded in code; CC/MCC Status: MCC). - Acute respiratory failure (J96.01) is validated by provider documentation of invasive mechanical ventilation attributed to respiratory failure or objective hypoxemia (RULE-Policy-Documents-DRG-Acute-Respiratory-Failure-with-Hypoxia.docx-b37, Presumption rule: When the provider documents initiation of invasive mechanical ventilation and attributes the need for ventilation to acute respiratory failure, Criterion 2 (objective hypoxemia measurement) is presumed satisfied...). Reasoning and corrections applied (line-level summary): - Principal diagnosis sequencing error: R65.21 (severe sepsis with septic shock) is properly coded as an additional/MCC, but policy requires the principal diagnosis to be the sepsis code A40.- or A41.- when sepsis/septic shock is the condition that occasioned admission. The medical record documents sepsis and identifies organisms (Group A Streptococcus and MRSA) (evidence: ED note n8; critical care n11; discharge summary n1030). Therefore L03.119 (cellulitis unspecified limb) as billed principal is not correct sequencing; the claim should have an organism-specific sepsis code as principal (A41.02 is supported by MRSA positive cultures and the policy table specifying A41.02 for MRSA sepsis). Evidence: policy requiring A40/A41 principal (ev1) + cultures (ev4) + MRSA sepsis mapping (ev5) + clinical septic shock (ev2, ev3). - Remove duplication/less-specific cellulitis code L03.119: the chart documents right-thigh necrotizing fasciitis and a specific cellulitis of the right lower limb code (L03.116) - keep the specific laterality code and remove the unspecified L03.119 (evidence: H&P CT confirming necrotizing fasciitis ev8; discharge description of surgical wound and STSG ev6). - Organism/infection codes and organism-specification: billed A49.59, A49.02 and B95.62 are inconsistent with the sepsis coding rules. With positive cultures and documented sepsis, the correct approach is an organism-specific sepsis code (A41.02 for MRSA sepsis is supported by policy; when the sepsis code embeds organism, the separate B95.x is not needed) (ev4, ev5). Therefore remove A49.59, A49.02 and B95.62 and replace sequencing so that A41.02 is principal with R65.21 listed as the additional MCC. - I63.9 (cerebral infarction) is billed as MCC but the chart and discharge summary do not document an acute ischemic stroke in the hospital course or as a discharge diagnosis; discharge diagnoses list DKA, necrotizing fasciitis, septic shock, ARDS and AKI but not stroke (ev14). Remove I63.9. - Z99.11 (dependence on respirator) billed POA=N: the record documents prolonged ventilation and later trach-collar trials with ventilator liberation; at transfer the patient was on nasal cannula and tolerating trach-collar trials (ev7, ev3). Z99.11 (a status of dependence) is not supported as an active status at discharge - remove it. - Procedures: the record documents emergent intubation, multiple OR debridements (excisions of subcutaneous tissue/fascia and muscle), PICC placement and arterial/monitoring lines, and prolonged mechanical ventilation (>96 hours). These procedure codes are supported and kept (0BH17EZ, 0JBM0ZZ, 0KBQ0ZZ, 02HV33Z, 03HY32Z, 5A1D90Z). The billed 0HRJX73 (replacement of right upper leg skin with autologous tissue substitute, full thickness) is not supported - the chart documents a split-thickness skin graft (STSG), not a full-thickness autologous replacement (ev6, ev8). Remove 0HRJX73. The billed transfusion code 30280B1 (platelet transfusion) is not specifically documented (H&P lists a generic 'post-operative anemia requiring transfusion' but there is no documentation of platelet transfusion specifically), so 30280B1 is removed (ev10). Citations used behind each of the substantive changes are enumerated in evidence_cited. The corrected complete diagnosis and procedure lists are provided below in the formal code_decisions and revised_* sets.
result.rationale_letter: Re: DRG audit determination - Claim MR_29 Dear Provider/Health Information Management Team, We audited the inpatient DRG coding for MR_29 (admission beginning 2026-11-10) against the medical record and governing DRG coding policies. After a three-way review (claim lines, record documentation, and sepsis/respiratory/stroke policy), we have determined there is a Finding requiring correction of principal diagnosis sequencing and removal of unsupported codes. Finding: Principal diagnosis sequencing error - severe sepsis/septic shock was not sequenced with the appropriate organism-specific sepsis principal code. The record documents septic shock on presentation with vasopressor support and intubation, elevated lactate, and positive deep tissue cultures growing Streptococcus pyogenes (Group A) and methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA). Policy for R65.21 (severe sepsis with septic shock) requires reporting R65.21 only as an additional code alongside A40.- or A41.- as the principal diagnosis. The record therefore supports an organism-specific A40/A41 sepsis principal code rather than the billed L03.119 (cellulitis unspecified limb). Basis (specific items relied on): - ED provider documentation of intubation and vasopressor support on arrival, with clinical recognition of septic shock (NOTE-Medical-Records-16-30-MR_29.pdf-n8). (Support for coding sepsis/septic shock.) - Critical care documentation of markedly elevated lactate and P/F ratio consistent with organ dysfunction due to sepsis (NOTE-Medical-Records-16-30-MR_29.pdf-n11). (Supports R65.21 and acute respiratory failure.) - Microbiology/hospital course documenting deep tissue cultures positive for Group A Streptococcus and MRSA (NOTE-Medical-Records-16-30-MR_29.pdf-n1030). (Supports organism-specific sepsis coding.) - Policy: R65.21 must be reported with A40.- or A41.- as the principal diagnosis (RULE-Policy-Documents-DRG-Sepsis-and-Septic-Shock.docx-b16). The policy shows A41.02 as the correct MRSA-sepsis code when MRSA is identified (RULE-Policy-Documents-DRG-Sepsis-and-Septic-Shock.docx-b81-r5). Correction applied (claim-level): - Principal diagnosis changed from L03.119 to A41.02 (sepsis due to MRSA) with R65.21 retained as the additional MCC (severe sepsis with septic shock). This sequencing aligns with the sepsis policy requirement that R65.21 be additional to an A40/A41 principal diagnosis. - Removed duplicate/less-specific cellulitis L03.119 (kept the specific right-lower-limb code L03.116). - Removed organism/site specification codes and B95.x that are redundant or inconsistent with organism-specific sepsis code (A49.59, A49.02, B95.62) because the sepsis code embeds the causative organism. - Removed I63.9 (cerebral infarction) - not documented in the chart or discharge diagnoses. - Removed Z99.11 (dependence on respirator) - the record documents prolonged ventilation with later successful weaning to trach-collar and nasal cannula on transfer (not ventilator-dependent at discharge). - Procedures: kept intubation, debridement excision codes, PICC and monitoring device, and prolonged ventilation (>96 hours); removed the billed full-thickness autologous skin replacement (0HRJX73) because the record documents a split-thickness skin graft. Removed platelet transfusion code 30280B1 because charted transfusion is described generically without documentation of platelet product administration. Corrected code lists and line-level decisions (enclosed) show the complete corrected diagnosis and procedure sets for the encounter. If you disagree with the clinical documentation interpretation, or you have source documentation not included in the record we reviewed (e.g., an operative report specifying a full-thickness graft or a MAR showing platelet transfusion), please provide that documentation for re-review within 30 days. Sincerely, Clinical Claims Auditor

code_decisions.reason: Unspecified cellulitis (L03.119) is redundant/less specific compared with documented right-thigh necrotizing fasciitis and the specific right-lower-limb cellulitis code (L03.116). Chart documents necrotizing fasciitis and STSG rather than an unspecified cellulitis.

Organism identified by culture and provider-documented sepsis requires an A40.-/A41.- sepsis principal code per policy; A49.59 (other streptococcal infection) is not the correct sequencing for sepsis with identified organism.
Septic shock documented with vasopressors and elevated lactate; R65.21 is supported and retains MCC status but must be additional to an A40.-/A41.- principal diagnosis.
Severe diabetic ketoacidosis on presentation is documented (pH 6.98); E11.10 supported.
Acidosis documented in DKA (pH 6.98); code supported as a metabolic derangement.
Acute respiratory failure with hypoxia is supported by documentation of invasive mechanical ventilation for respiratory failure and objective hypoxemia/P/F ratios; J96.01 is validated and MCC.
ARDS is documented as a complication of the course with compatible imaging (bilateral opacities) and severe hypoxemia; POA flagged N (developed during stay) is consistent with chart.
Acute kidney injury documented by nephrology with creatinine peak and attribution to DKA/sepsis/contrast; N17.9 supported.
MRSA organism was identified in cultures; policy supports use of organism-specific sepsis A41.02 rather than a non-sepsis A49.02 site-unspecified infection code when coding sepsis.
When MRSA sepsis is coded as A41.02 the organism is embedded in the sepsis code and a separate B95.62 causal organism code is not required per the policy guidance.
Cellulitis of right lower limb / necrotizing fasciitis of the right thigh and subsequent wound care are documented; keep the specific laterality code L03.116.
Diabetes with hyperglycemia and endocrinology involvement are documented; E11.65 supported.

Diabetic chronic kidney disease (E11.22) is billed but chart documents contrast-induced AKI with recovery and does not document chronic diabetic CKD in the admission/discharge problem list; insufficient documentation for E11.22.
Diabetic neuropathy is documented in the history/problem list; E11.40 supported.
Essential hypertension is documented in the problem list and discharge diagnoses; keep.
Hyperlipidemia is documented in the discharge diagnoses and problem list.
Depression is documented in the chart/problem list with psychiatry follow-up; F32.9 supported.
Dependence on respirator status is not supported at transfer/discharge (patient on nasal cannula and tolerating trach-collar trials); status code for ongoing ventilator dependence is not supported.
No documentation of an acute ischemic cerebral infarction appears in the admission/discharge problem lists or hospital course; discharge diagnoses do not list stroke. I63.9 is unsupported.
Endotracheal intubation is documented in the ED/ICU for respiratory failure and is supported by the record.
Surgical excision/debridement of subcutaneous tissue/fascia of the right thigh is supported by emergent OR debridement documentation for necrotizing fasciitis.
Excision of muscle (debridement) during operative necrotizing fasciitis management is documented; code supported.

Billed as replacement with autologous full-thickness tissue (0HRJX73) but record documents a split-thickness skin graft (STSG) performed on ICU day 18; full-thickness autologous replacement is not supported by the operative/course documentation.
PICC/infusion device into central venous circulation is supported by discharge documentation noting PICC in place for antibiotics.
Monitoring/arterial line placement is supported by ICU orders/monitoring requirements documented on admission.
Assistance with respiratory ventilation >96 consecutive hours is supported by documented prolonged mechanical ventilation, trach-collar weaning protocol, and extended ICU course.

Chart documents 'post-operative anemia requiring transfusion' but does not document platelet transfusion specifically; code for transfusion of nonautologous platelets is unsupported in the notes reviewed.
